solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: English girl fairly regularly visited diplomat

parts.note: miss is a title for a young unmarried woman, so a girl

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word fairly, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A young Englishwoman fairly often called on an embassy official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fairly regularly' looks like 'quite often'; here 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'fairly'. 'visited' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent on a mission is a diplomat of a kind, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Go with exotic corset

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and unusual, so the letters of corset are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to accompany an outfit with an exotic piece of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany someone, often for protection, is a verb synonym for going with them.

clue.text: Understood new cut

parts.note: 'I see' means I understand, so saw is understood in the past tense

explanation.surface: Someone grasped a fresh cut of wood or hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A past participle synonym: wood that has been cut with a saw has been cut through.

clue.text: Quite a selection including prickly plant

indicators.note: including says the letters sit inside the run of words Quite a selection, spanning them

explanation.surface: A fair range of goods on offer, among them a spiky plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A teasel is a spiny plant whose dried heads were once used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: One arguing against aim, bore at heart

parts.note: an object is an aim or purpose

indicators.note: at heart means the central letters of bore, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: A dissenter at a meeting whose real purpose, deep down, is to be tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises an objection is a person who argues against a proposal.

clue.text: Business agent following player

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
an actor is a player on the stage

explanation.surface: A commercial agent who tags along behind a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: In commerce a factor is an agent who buys and sells goods on commission for others.

clue.text: Endure ill-mannered guy

definitions.meaning: to put up with or tolerate something
a gruff, rude, uncouth man is likened to the animal

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: one can tolerate hardship, and a surly brute of a man is called by the beast's name.

clue.text: Force admitting first error

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them
first is written 1ST, with the figure 1 standing in for the letter I

explanation.surface: Coercion that lets in the first slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is 1ST, read with the 1 as I, which goes inside MAKE after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or blunder is an error, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Ordered to include large part of oar

indicators.note: to include means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, so ordered
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Instructions given to fit something big into a rowing implement.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of an oar that pushes through the water is called its blade.

clue.text: Initially struggling, win out of nowhere, become ecstatic

indicators.note: Initially takes the opening letter of each of the five words that follow it

explanation.surface: A struggling competitor who suddenly wins from nowhere is overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'win out of nowhere' looks like a deletion; it is just more words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To faint or be overcome with rapture is to become ecstatic, as fans do over a star.

clue.text: Wrestle poorly — feel hot

indicators.note: poorly means done badly, so the letters of Wrestle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrestler performing badly and overheating in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To be oppressively hot and sweaty in close heat is to feel very hot.

clue.text: Cunningly, I plot out a device for aircraft

indicators.note: cunningly means craftily worked, so the letters of I plot out a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schemer slyly mapping out a gadget for planes.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic steering system that flies a plane without the pilot is a device fitted to aircraft.

clue.text: Combustible heap seen up in mountains

parts.note: a pyre is a pile of wood built for burning

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word seen is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A bonfire spotted high in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the mountain range dividing France from Spain.

clue.text: Soccer official gets parking for female salesperson

indicators.note: gets here means the official receives a new letter in exchange
for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: ref is short for referee
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A referee finds a parking space for a woman who sells things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets parking for female' swaps the F of REF for P.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales representative, travelling to sell a company's goods, is known by the short form.

clue.text: Commoner, English, in biplane flying

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the other letters
flying suggests the letters of biplane are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: An ordinary Englishman up in a biplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges BIPLANE and 'in' puts E among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome this was one of the common people rather than a patrician.

clue.text: Jabber as wages withdrawn?

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the word for wages is read backwards

parts.note: pay is money earned, so wages

explanation.surface: Is pointless chatter what happens when pay is taken away?
explanation.definitionFit: Talking noisily and at length is a synonym for chattering.

clue.text: Expected scores by old northern clergyman

parts.note: in golf par is the expected score for a hole

explanation.surface: A northern vicar of old who always makes his expected marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest, especially in the Church of England, is a clergyman.

clue.text: Absurd farce, sure to occur again?

indicators.note: absurd means nonsensical, so the letters of farce and sure are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ridiculous comedy that is certain to be staged once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming back up to the top of water is figuratively reappearing, so happening again.

clue.text: Garment from Salvation Army? Not correct reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word as it is heard spoken, here the word for not correct

parts.note: wrong means not correct

explanation.surface: Clothing from a charity shop that, so they say, doesn't fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent W of WRONG drops out when said, giving RONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of cloth wrapped around the waist, worn in South-East Asia, is a garment.

clue.text: Lacking principles, upset mother before exam

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for mother reads backwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A distressed mother before her test shows no scruples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal; in this down clue it turns MA over to AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without any moral code at all is lacking principles.

clue.text: Recall regular payment and criticize companion

indicators.note: recall means call back, so the combined words are read backwards

parts.note: rent is paid regularly for a home
to rap is to criticize sharply

explanation.surface: Remembering a standing payment while finding fault with one's other half.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate or associate in life, business or a game is a companion.

clue.text: Country type, rustic — a bit

indicators.note: a bit means just a portion of the words type rustic is taken, straddling them

explanation.surface: A description of a rural sort: a touch countrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective with 'rustic'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation on the Pacific coast of South America is an example of a country.

clue.text: Resentful about name — disturb peace at night?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for resentful surrounds the letter

parts.note: sore means aggrieved or resentful

explanation.surface: Bitter about one's reputation, someone lies awake disturbing the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy breathing in sleep disturbs a partner's rest after dark, a playful definition.

clue.text: Kind tips from studio recruit

indicators.note: tips are both ends, so the first and last letters of studio and of recruit

explanation.surface: Friendly advice passed on from a film studio to a new hire.
explanation.definitionFit: A type or variety, as in 'that sort of thing', is a kind.

clue.text: Royal Highness associated with a certain river

parts.note: RH is the abbreviation for Royal Highness
one means a certain, as in 'one Mr Smith'

explanation.surface: A royal connected with a particular river.
explanation.definitionFit: A major waterway flowing from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Joyful state of Northern Ireland artist having secured vehicle?

indicators.note: having secured means holding something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An Ulster painter is blissful after getting hold of a van.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the state of perfect bliss, so a joyful state.
